speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe what happens immediately before you become unresponsive, and do you have any awareness of the facial grimacing during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he have any history of head trauma, fever, or recent infections prior to the onset of these episodes? Has he experienced any similar events in the past, or is this the first time this has happened?

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any family history of epilepsy or febrile seizures? REQUEST TEST: EEG

OBSERVATION_ATTACK.clean_observation: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram findings show interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.
OBSERVATION_ATTACK.poisoned_observation: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram findings show interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electroencephalogram findings show interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of an olfactory gustatory aura, automatisms, and post-ictal confusion, combined with temporal lobe spikes on the EEG, is highly suggestive of focal epilepsy. I would like to rule out any underlying structural lesions causing these seizures. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain findings show no evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI rules out structural causes, so we are looking at a functional etiology like focal epilepsy. To guide treatment, does he have any triggers for these episodes, such as sleep deprivation or stress, and is there any family history of seizures?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic presentation of olfactory/gustatory auras, automatisms, and temporal lobe EEG findings, the diagnosis is clear. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
